approachQuestion.prompt:
Nearest inspection point

Given a read-only array of n integer points and a query point Q, return the zero-based index of the point nearest to Q in Euclidean distance. On a tie return the smallest index. Duplicate points are allowed.

Example 1: points=[(3,4),(-3,4),(1,1)],Q=(0,0) -> 2.
Example 2: points=[(1,0),(-1,0)],Q=(0,0) -> 0.

Constraints and assumptions: 1 <= n <= 200000; all coordinates including Q are integers in [-10^9,10^9]. Do not reorder or modify points. Return one index; exact tie handling is required. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Scan in index order, comparing exact squared distances to Q. Update the best index only on a strict decrease.
options.feedback: Squaring preserves the order of nonnegative Euclidean distances. Strict updates preserve the earliest index on ties, and the maximum squared distance is 8*10^18, within signed 64-bit.

options.text: Store every exact squared distance in an auxiliary array, then scan it for the first minimum.
options.feedback: It returns the correct earliest index, but a running best avoids the distance array.

options.text: Minimize abs(dx)+abs(dy) instead, using the same tie rule.
options.feedback: For Q=(0,0), points=[(3,0),(2,2)], it returns 0 although point 1 has the smaller Euclidean distance.

options.text: Compare exact squared distances but replace the best index on less-than-or-equal.
options.feedback: For points=[(1,0),(-1,0)],Q=(0,0), it returns 1 rather than the required earliest index 0.

feedback.reason: Compare squared Euclidean distances exactly while preserving the earliest-index tie rule.
details: Scan indices in increasing order. Compute dx*dx+dy*dy in signed 64-bit arithmetic; replace the saved best index only for a strictly smaller squared distance.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (squared-distance-scan). Let n be the point count. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Scan every point once with one saved best squared distance and index.
details: Every point is inspected once, since the last point may be uniquely nearest. Each squared-distance computation uses constant work; the best index, distance and current differences are constant state. The read-only input is neither sorted nor copied.
